name: China, Road Traffic Safety Law art. 44 and its Implementing Regulations art. 38, 51, 52 (right-hand traffic)
status: draft: rules taken from the text of the Implementing Regulations (State Council order 405 of 2004, revised 2017-10-07), checked on 2026-10-30 against a published copy, not the official gazette. Not validated on any data. Article 52 lists its rules without saying how they combine when two apply; the order here is the article's order. Confirm with a local traffic-law expert before using results.
notes: Law art. 44: at a junction without lights, signs, markings or a police officer, slow down and let pedestrians and vehicles with priority go first.

Reg. 52 (no light, no police officer): (1) where signs or markings control the junction, the side they give priority goes first; (2) otherwise stop and look before entering and yield to vehicles coming from the road on the right (yield_right); (3) a turning vehicle yields to one going straight (turner_yields_straight); (4) of two vehicles from opposite directions, the right turner yields to the left turner (oncoming_right_yields_left, the opposite of Germany's StVO 9(4)).
Reg. 52 has no rule for a road that ends at a T junction (t_junction none): without a sign, yield_right decides there too.

Reg. 52 has no arrival-order rule. A junction with a stop sign (停车让行) on every approach is therefore decided like an unsigned one (first_arrival false; every pair goes through tie_rules, and unknown_order does not apply).

Reg. 51(7) (signalised junction without arrow lights): a turning vehicle yields to vehicles going straight and to pedestrians, and an oncoming right turner yields to a left turner: green_rules, applied when both have a circular green. Reg. 38(1): on green, turning vehicles must not obstruct the released straight-on traffic.
No specific article on entering from a driveway or private ground was checked. The CAT code's driveway rule (the one entering from off the road yields) is kept as it is.
Roundabouts (Reg. 51(2): yield to vehicles already in the roundabout) are not modelled.

Reg. 38(1): on red, a right-turning vehicle may proceed if it does not obstruct the released vehicles and pedestrians; no stop is required. Reg. 40 and 41: a red arrow (or red cross) forbids its lane or direction. Who must yield is still the red-light rule of the CAT code: the vehicle on red yields.

Road Traffic Safety Law (2021) art. 47(1): passing a crosswalk, slow down; when a pedestrian is crossing on it, stop and give way. Supreme People's Court Guiding Case No. 90 (Bei Huifeng v. Haining traffic police): a pedestrian walking or staying on the crosswalk is given way to, unless the pedestrian clearly signals the vehicle to go first; whether one is crossing is read from the pedestrian's behaviour over a span of time (crosswalk 'on').

Art. 47(2): on a road without traffic signals, when a pedestrian crosses the road, the vehicle avoids them (unsignalised_road 'yield': a duty to give way even off a crosswalk). Art. 62: the pedestrian crosses where there is no crosswalk only after making sure it is safe.

Implementing Regulations art. 38(1)(1): on green, turning vehicles must not obstruct released straight-on vehicles and pedestrians (turning_yields_to_pedestrians, turning_yields_to_cyclists: non-motor vehicles are vehicles). Art. 38(3): where a junction has no pedestrian or non-motor signals, pedestrians and non-motor vehicles follow the motor-vehicle lights.
No statutory lateral distance for overtaking a cyclist or pedestrian (art. 43; regulations art. 47 speak only of a sufficient safe distance): passing_m null, the screen's physical fallback applies.
Driving across a sidewalk out of private ground: no specific article was found (sidewalk_crossing 'care').
